---
title: "Distribution and utility verification"
---

phit's [distribution functions](../distributions.qmd) are compared with base R, SciPy, and 60-digit mpmath values. The table below is generated from the [saved comparison report](distributions-results.json) by `python3 scripts/distribution-docs.py`. Shared metrics are described in [Verification](../verification.qmd).

## Compared

Densities and masses, CDFs, survival functions, their logs, and quantiles for 13 families, at saved parameter sets and evaluation points that include tiny probabilities, large counts and shapes, support boundaries, and point masses. Expected values are fixed in advance and are never chosen by looking at the native result.

<!-- END REFERENCE EVIDENCE -->

The table uses finite, nonzero mpmath reference values and excludes quantile
endpoints. Logs use error divided by max(1, |reference|), ordinary densities and
probabilities use relative error (a normal-range floor for subnormal references),
and quantiles use relative error with a `1e-300` floor. Zero/support/degenerate
endpoints are checked separately below, rather than exaggerated by dividing a
small absolute difference by an artificial tiny scale.

Typical native errors are below `1e-13`. The worst saved native case is about
`8.34e-13`, in a large-df chi-square log tail, where cdflib's large-shape regime
sets the accuracy. R is somewhat better on that case. These are observed errors on
the tested inputs, not a bound for every shape, scale, or tail.

## Inputs and references

`tests/generate-distribution-fixtures.R` produces 553 distribution cases: R d/p/q
functions at saved explicit parameter sets and evaluation points, including tiny
probabilities, large counts/shapes, support boundaries and point masses. The same
generator writes eight univariate, three paired and two weighted descriptive cases
using seed 20261012. Numeric JSON inputs are parsed with serde_json float-roundtrip
support so that Rust and PHP use the intended binary64 values.

`docs/verifications/compare_distributions.py` evaluates closed-form densities and
regularized incomplete-beta/gamma tails using mpmath at 60 digits. Continuous
reference quantiles use independently evaluated log-tail Newton iterations,
starting from native/R/SciPy candidates but accepting only a high-precision tail
residual. Discrete references verify the CDF-step inequality. Values are rounded
once to binary64. A computation timeout or unavailable reference is recorded as
null, never replaced by the native value. The 27 unavailable points remain visible
in the report; their ordinary tests use the saved R reference and explicit identities.
Subnormal values have fewer significant bits, so relative-error claims are limited.

The [provenance manifest](reference-manifest.json) indexes all R/SciPy/mpmath and
descriptive inputs, quantities, versions, generators, tolerance policies and hashes.
The independent reference fixture SHA-256 values are also recorded in the native
refresh report. `--stored-references` re-evaluates PHP without changing those values.

```sh
# Intentional independent reference regeneration (may take substantial time):
Rscript tests/generate-distribution-fixtures.R
PHP=/path/to/matching/php .context/v02/python/bin/python docs/verifications/compare_distributions.py
# Routine native refresh against existing references:
PHP=/path/to/matching/php .context/v02/python/bin/python docs/verifications/compare_distributions.py --stored-references
python3 scripts/reference-manifest.py
python3 scripts/distribution-docs.py
```

The optional Python environment needs NumPy, SciPy and mpmath; pins are in
`tests/benchmarks/distribution-requirements.txt`. None are extension runtime or
offline-test dependencies.

## Tolerance and checks

| Quantity | Absolute/relative test tolerance |
| --- | --- |
| Density, mass, CDF and SF | `1e-300 + 1e-12 * abs(reference)` |
| Log density/mass/tails | `1e-12 * max(1, abs(reference))` |
| Distribution quantiles | `1e-15 + 1e-12 * abs(reference)` |
| Descriptive R quantities | Relative `1e-12`, exact zero |

`tests/distributions.php` performs 8,618 comparisons under these original
tolerances. When saved R and mpmath differ beyond tolerance, it uses the immutable
mpmath value (25 independently adjudicated points). Forty-three documented boundary
differences have separate conventions/identity checks. Scalar/batch values must be
identical, including NAN/INF conventions where applicable. The suite also checks
CDF/SF sums, quantile inverses and monotonicity, direct log functions, degenerate
cases, argument names/defaults, array order and invalid input/error categories.
An overflowing size-plus-mean NB conversion is checked to avoid a false point mass.

Rust independently checks extreme Student-t quantiles against mpmath, probability
identities, validation and scaled-density underflow. A diagnostic Rust test
reports raw worst errors against R, including the intended differences listed below.

`tests/descriptive.php` adds 145 R comparisons and missing/error checks.
`crates/stats-core/tests/descriptive.rs` covers the same stored examples plus
overflow and degenerate cases. [Descriptive statistics](../descriptive.qmd)
explains the sample, population, frequency, and reliability definitions.

## Known exceptions

- Discrete quantile p=1 for a point mass returns its mass location. R/SciPy may
  instead return the generic upper-support bound, including infinity.
- R's F density at +INF is NAN; the native API returns zero there.
- R F quantiles can round to zero for tiny probabilities and small numerator df,
  where the native/mpmath value is a representable positive value.
- R's Student-t quantile at df=0.5 has a small nonzero center and selected far-tail
  inaccuracies. Native centering and high-precision tail checks establish the
  chosen values.
- R's discrete-quantile probability adjustment near `1 - 2^-52` can shift the
  returned count. Native uses a relative `64*EPSILON` allowance on the smaller tail.
- R's mean-form negative-binomial mass approximation for size much larger than
  the observed count differs from the independent high-precision calculation.
- SciPy's large-df chi-square CDF has about `8.16e-9` relative error at the saved
  five-standard-deviation lower-tail point. The native and R results match mpmath
  much more closely. The [benchmark](../benchmarks/distributions.qmd) records the
  same peer discrepancy without weakening native comparison tolerances.

Raw values and per-point errors remain in the fixtures and the report. Intentional
conventions and peer-library errors are kept separate from unavailable reference points.

## Reproduction

See the commands under [Inputs and references](#inputs-and-references) and run
`./scripts/check` with a matching PHP for the full suite.

## Implementation history: backend and model-path audit

The [raw statrs report](distributions-audit.json) and executable
`crates/stats-core/examples/statrs_audit.rs` document why statrs alone is not used
for the new distribution API. The [reuse experiment](distributions-reuse.json)
compares the public Normal log-CDF and Student-t quantile with the existing probit
and OLS formulas. Candidate t quantiles improve large-df reference error, but all
six tested critical values and 17 tested normal log-CDF values differ in rounding,
so the regression code keeps its existing paths.

```sh
cargo run -p stats-core --release --locked --example statrs_audit
cargo run -p stats-core --release --locked --example distribution_reuse_audit
PHP=/path/to/matching/php PHP_CONFIG=/path/to/php-config ./scripts/check
```

The [v0.2 assessment](../v0.2.qmd) is the historical record of that release's scope.
